work_order.confidence_rationale: I re-derived the load-bearing claims myself rather than accepting the proposal's, and re-executed its central claim: a scratch vitest spec in packages/loot-core, run and then deleted, confirms that for {start: today, frequency: 'monthly', endMode: 'after_n_occurrences', endOccurrences: 1} scheduleIsRecurring returns true while getNextDateAfter returns null — so the UI offers an action setNextDate silently drops — and the same split for a past on_date end. I then wrote the proposed scheduleIsSkippable body verbatim and ran it against seven contract cases of my own construction, all green, including both UI-shaped fixtures. I confirmed by reading that there are exactly four skip-eligibility sites plus three inverted canBeCompleted readers plus one preview reader and no fifth site anywhere in packages/; that ScheduleEditForm.tsx:134 is the only unguarded nullable string input among siblings already carrying || ''; that all four call sites already select '*' with non-optional next_date; that SchedulesTable's Complete is gated on status alone; and that the e2e duplication is as described (grep -c tableOptions = 2, grep -c 'as unknown as' = 2). I verified the brief's required correction against SchedulesTable.tsx:196/:202/:208 and the e2e comment at :358 rather than treating it as settled. Not higher for two reasons no amount of reading retires: the four e2e hygiene edits are entirely unexecuted and gate nothing in CI, and AC-1's browser recipe stops one interaction short of having been driven end to end — the picker's popover gating is read from source, not watched. If that recipe turns out to be wrong, AC-1 stalls and the ticket's one behavioural fix goes unverified; that is the single most likely thing I have wrong. One green QA pass over steps 4-6 would move this into the 90s.
work_order.understanding:
Issue #61 bundles eight follow-ups from PR #59 (merged as 0fb77b4): five e2e-test hygiene items, three QA findings of which two are real defects and one does not hold. I re-derived the load-bearing claims from the code and re-executed the reproduction myself rather than taking the proposal's word for it.

Real: review 1 (the page model returns a lazy Locator read with non-retrying count()/allTextContents()), review 2 (the test builds payee locators at :340-347 then asserts against raw indices 2 and 3 at :360/:369 under an index-independence comment), review 4 (two byte-for-byte identical 12-key $send('query') envelopes at :24-37 and :136-155 — grep -c tableOptions returns 2), review 5 (redundant open/dismiss/re-open). Not a change to this repo: review 3 (PR #59 is merged, 0fb77b4 already carries [AI], .github/** is forbidden).

QA 1 is real and I reproduced it by execution in this arbiter session: for {start: today, frequency: 'monthly', endMode: 'after_n_occurrences', endOccurrences: 1}, scheduleIsRecurring returns true while getNextDateAfter returns null — and likewise for a past on_date end. QA 3 is real with a one-line cause at ScheduleEditForm.tsx:134. QA 2 does not hold: runMutator is a single serialised queue every mutating handler shares, including via the API.

work_order.root_cause: Three distinct causes. (1) The UI and the write ask different questions: four skip-eligibility sites call scheduleIsRecurring ('is this a recurrence at all?') while setNextDate asks the strictly stronger 'does getNextDateAfter return a date?', which is false once the recurrence is exhausted. PR #59 introduced the weaker predicate, so the UI offers an action the server silently drops. (2) ScheduleFormFields.name is nullable by type and seeded to null (useScheduleEdit.ts:266), and ScheduleEditForm.tsx:134 renders it into a controlled Input without the || '' guard its siblings at :159 and :175 already carry — the only unguarded nullable string pass-through in the file. (3) The e2e page model returns a lazy Locator that consumers read with non-retrying calls, the test grew a second index-based path alongside the payee-based one, plus a duplicated AQL envelope and a redundant open/dismiss cycle.
work_order.approach: Three changes in dependency order. (A) Add scheduleIsSkippable(dateCond, nextDate) to loot-core shared/schedules.ts: false on null/undefined nextDate, else scheduleIsRecurring(dateCond) && getNextDateAfter(dateCond, nextDate) != null. It reuses getNextDateAfter rather than reimplementing occurrence logic, so the UI predicate and the setNextDate write are driven by the same function and cannot drift — that reuse is the fix, not an implementation detail. A new function rather than a widened scheduleIsRecurring, because three sites read that predicate inverted for Complete and computeSchedulePreviewTransactions uses it for preview expansion. Then swap the four skip-eligibility call sites, passing the row's next_date; all four already select '*' and hold the full entity. SchedulesTable's Complete item is left exactly as it is. (B) value={fields.name || ''} at ScheduleEditForm.tsx:134, matching :159 and :175; the reducer's initial null is left alone since it is read for truthiness. (C) e2e hygiene: await expect(menu).toBeVisible() once inside _openNthScheduleMenu so all three consumers inherit the wait; widen three helpers' row parameter to number | Locator so the existing payee locators replace the raw indices; hoist a module-level Node-side aqlQuery<T> owning the duplicated envelope, with the split-transfer test's queries moving Node-side through it (page.evaluate is serialised and cannot close over a Node binding, so the rule-get/rule-update block stays browser-side taking plain serialisable arguments); delete the redundant open/count-0/Escape block; add a console assertion modelled on command-bar.test.ts, regex-filtered to the two React warning texts.

out_of_scope: Review 3 — retitling PR #59 with the [AI] prefix. The premise has expired: PR #59 is merged and 0fb77b4 already carries [AI], so history is compliant. The fix would be `gh pr edit`, and .github/** is a forbidden path.

QA 2 — two concurrent skips advancing next_date twice. The stated cause does not exist: one serialised queue that every mutating handler shares, including via the API. The stated fix (compare-and-swap) would turn two legitimate sequential skips into one, trading a cosmetic double-advance for a real lost action.

The reframed residual from QA 2: a retry of schedule/skip-next-date after a timeout advances next_date twice. Closing it needs a caller-supplied idempotency key or server-side dedupe — a new handler argument, a decision about sync replay, and a change to the undo boundary. A feature, not a small fix.

Three sites read it inverted for Complete and computeSchedulePreviewTransactions uses it for preview expansion, where 'is this recurring?' is the right question. One predicate cannot serve both. Guarded explicitly by AC-2.

Making the Schedules row menu's Complete mutually exclusive with Skip, which is what v2's AC-2 asserted. The code does not do this today and the e2e test at :358-365 depends on a due recurring row showing five items. Changing it would alter Complete's behaviour, which no finding raises. AC-2 is restated to guard the real invariant instead.

Making setNextDate report the no-op instead of dropping it (QA's suggested alternative). It changes a handler's return contract and the API surface to fix a menu-visibility question better answered where the question is asked; the null guard is load-bearing and asserted by an existing test.

Adding a component test for the ScheduleEditForm null guard. ScheduleEditForm pulls in useScheduleEdit, which needs live queries, redux and modals, and no existing desktop-client component test mounts anything that heavy. The console assertion plus AC-4 cover it at a fraction of the setup.
Enabling Playwright in CI so the e2e hygiene work gates something. That is a change to .sdlc/config.yml and .github/workflows, both forbidden paths.

alternatives_considered.approach: Follow QA 1's stated remedy: drop setNextDate's `newNextDate != null` guard and surface the no-op to the caller instead.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It fixes the wrong layer. The null guard is load-bearing — getNextDateAfter legitimately returns null for an exhausted recurrence and an existing test at schedules.test.ts:1042-1050 asserts it — so removing it would write null into schedules_next_date. The UI needs eligibility up front regardless, since a client cannot learn from an absent error that an action was dropped.

alternatives_considered.approach: Fix QA 1 by teaching scheduleIsRecurring itself to check for a remaining occurrence, leaving the four call sites untouched.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Smaller diff, wrong answer. Three sites read the predicate inverted for Complete and computeSchedulePreviewTransactions uses it for preview expansion, where 'is this recurring?' is the right question. One predicate cannot serve both.

alternatives_considered.approach: Fix QA 2 as reported, with a compare-and-swap on schedules_next_date keyed on the next_date that was read.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: There is no race for it to close — runMutator is a single serialised queue, so the second skip legitimately reads the first's committed write. A CAS would make a user's second deliberate skip do nothing and silently lose a client retry.

alternatives_considered.approach: For review 2 and 5, delete the payee locators and the index-independence comment and keep the raw indices, on the grounds that they are correct today and fail loudly on drift.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The reviewer already granted the indices are correct; the objection is that the comment claims a guarantee the test does not keep. Deleting the locators removes the better mechanism to satisfy the weaker one.

alternatives_considered.approach: For review 4, hoist only the 12-key envelope object to module scope and spread it into both page.evaluate callbacks.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It does not work. A page.evaluate callback is serialised into the browser and cannot reference a Node-scope binding, so the spread would throw a ReferenceError. Deduplication requires a Node-side function that owns its own evaluate, and the split-transfer test's remaining rule-get/rule-update block has to take its data in as plain arguments.

alternatives_considered.approach: Fix QA 3 in useScheduleEdit by seeding the reducer's initial state with name: '' instead of null.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: A wider edit with no behavioural gain — name is read for truthiness where '' and null are both falsy — and it touches the state contract rather than the render site, where lines 159 and 175 already establish the codebase's convention.

alternatives_considered.approach: Make Complete and Skip mutually exclusive on the Schedules row menu, so v2's original AC-2 becomes true.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: This is what the brief's rejection forbids and the code confirms: it would change Complete's behaviour on every recurring schedule, which no finding asks for, and it would contradict the e2e test this plan edits — schedules.test.ts:358-365 depends on a due recurring row showing five items. The regression guard now states the real invariant instead.

alternatives_considered.approach: Ask for a scope_changed route so the two real defects split from the five e2e-hygiene items into separate tickets.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Considered as the arbiter and declined. The ticket is a follow-up bundle of one PR's review and QA findings, the split parts are individually small, and two planning rounds have already converged on this shape; splitting now would spend a round to produce two work orders covering fewer lines than the single one. Recorded here rather than requested so the reasoning is visible if a human disagrees.

assumptions: verify.e2e is empty and desktop-client's vitest include excludes e2e/, so no Playwright assertion in this plan gates CI. Read from both configs and the workflow; the workflow was not run.
scheduleIsRecurring has exactly the call sites grep found, and scheduleIsSkippable is added alongside rather than replacing any of them.

All four skip-eligibility sites hold the full schedule entity from a select('*') query, so next_date is in hand, and ScheduleEntity.next_date is non-optional. I read each call site and each query; not verified at runtime that a row's next_date is never null, but the predicate short-circuits on null regardless.
The @actual-app/api send path reaches the same runHandler the desktop client does, which is what makes QA 2's diagnosis wrong. Traced through api/methods.ts and the server receiver but not executed.
A React controlled input given value={null} produces both recorded warnings. Standard React behaviour corroborated by the file's sibling guards, but not observed in a browser here.

The Schedules table keeps a saved 'for 1 occurrence' schedule with next_date set to today rather than culling it. Every control in the recipe exists and the resulting config was executed against the real predicates, but this save-to-table step is unobserved.
unknowns: Whether the Schedules table has a schedule count large enough for the extra getNextDateAfter call per row per render to matter. No budget-size data, no profiling; React Compiler may memoise it. The risk is stated but unmeasured.

Whether some other caller — a plugin, a script, an importer — constructs a recur condition with an exhausted end and depends on Skip being offered. Grep found only the four UI sites and computeSchedulePreviewTransactions, but plugins live outside this repository.
Whether the reviewer would accept the console-assertion addition to the e2e test as belonging in this ticket, or as scope creep on a file that already carries four changes.

What the correct behaviour is for Complete on an exhausted recurrence — whether it too is a silent no-op elsewhere. Left alone because no finding raises it; AC-2 records current behaviour as the thing to preserve, not as correct.
work_order.debate_summary:
There was no debate to arbitrate. plan/critique.json is an empty object — the critic wrote nothing — so this council's third round is a single-planner plan that I audited rather than arbitrated between. I am recording that plainly rather than manufacturing agreement. The findings below are my own verification and my own edits, not the critic's.

What the brief's rejection changed, and what I checked about it. The brief records a rejected v1 whose single required correction was that v2's AC-2, AC-5 and qa_script step 8 asserted a Complete/Skip mutual exclusivity the code does not produce. The v3 proposal claims it deleted that claim rather than qualifying it. I verified against the source rather than taking the claim: SchedulesTable.tsx:196/:202/:208 gate restart on status, skip on status-or-canSkip, and complete on status alone, so a recurring due schedule shows both items — and e2e/schedules.test.ts:357-365 already depends on that, its own comment saying the menu is asserted by name rather than by counting 'which a due recurring row legitimately fills to five'. The brief was right and the proposal fixed it properly. My one addition to AC-2 is the positive statement of the pairing that does hold, so the criterion is falsifiable in both directions rather than only in the direction the fix moves. I also noted in AC-5's how_to_verify that the bulk bar additionally requires every selected schedule to be skippable, which the criterion's phrasing did not account for.

What I re-executed. The proposal's central claim is that the UI offers an action the server silently drops, because scheduleIsRecurring and setNextDate's getNextDateAfter ask different questions. I did not take that on trust: I wrote a scratch vitest spec inside packages/loot-core and ran it. Seven tests, all passing, then deleted. It reproduces the split — for an after_n_occurrences-1 monthly recur starting today, scheduleIsRecurring true while getNextDateAfter null, and the same for a past on_date end — and it runs the proposed scheduleIsSkippable body against seven contract cases of my own construction. One of my seven initially failed, on a fixture I had guessed rather than copied; I replaced it with the shape the repo's own weeklyOnSaturday factory produces, after which it passed. That is worth saying plainly: my first failure was my fixture, exactly as the proposal reported about its own, and neither failure says anything about the predicate. reproduced:true is now backed by my own execution, not the proposer's word.

What I checked and did not change. I did not re-litigate QA 2. The drop rests on runMutator being a single serialised queue every mutating handler shares, including through the API path, which I traced through mutators.ts, shared/async.ts and the handler registration; the reasoning holds and QA observed precisely what serialised execution produces. I kept the decision to add scheduleIsSkippable rather than widen scheduleIsRecurring, which AC-2 now guards explicitly. I kept all four files[] edits to the four skip-eligibility sites as the proposal has them; I read each call site and each query and confirmed s.next_date is in scope at every one, so the signature change compiles without widening a query.

My own edits. (1) I promoted one thing out of risks and into files[]: the proposal decided to add a sentence to scheduleIsRecurring's own doc comment saying it does not answer the skip question, and named that decision in risks[2] and residual_risks[4] — but never put it in files[], so an implementer working from the file list would have dropped it, and it is the mitigation for the two-predicate hazard the proposal itself calls the sharpest remaining one. It is now the second half of the schedules.ts entry. (2) I added one clause to AC-2 making the Skip/Complete coexistence on the Schedules row menu part of the check, since a criterion that only says 'Complete unchanged' would pass just as well if the change had removed Complete from every recurring schedule by accident. (3) I added the bulk-bar nuance to AC-5. (4) I added a risk naming a consequence of the fix that is not a regression: on the three transaction-side menus an exhausted recurrence selected alone will now offer neither Complete nor Skip, because canBeCompleted is !scheduleIsRecurring and an exhausted recurrence is still a recur. That behaviour is unchanged, but QA hitting an empty menu could reasonably call it a bug, and it should be expected rather than discovered.

Where I disagree with the proposal. Its confidence_rationale says the previous round's error was 'argued' rather than verified and presents v3 as having verified it. I verified it too, and it holds — but I do not treat 'v2 got this wrong once' as strong evidence that v3 will survive review intact. The error was a real one, made in the last round, on the same file, about the same menu. That is a reason to read AC-2 and the SchedulesTable diff carefully during review, and it is why I did not raise the score on the strength of the correction alone.

One thing I considered and declined. This ticket bundles two real defects with five e2e-hygiene items, which is arguably two tickets. I did not request a scope_changed route: the parts are individually small, the bundle is a single PR's follow-ups, and two rounds have converged on this shape. The reasoning is recorded in alternatives_considered so a human can disagree with me cheaply. I also omitted route_request — the route [plan, implement, review, qa] already contains review and qa, and I found nothing in the code that needs a stage it lacks.

Residual disagreement I did not resolve. Two closely-named predicates with different meanings now coexist, and the doc comments mitigate the hazard without eliminating it; a future reader who collapses them reintroduces this bug. I kept the decision, and record it as a live hazard (residual_risks[4]) rather than agreeing it is tidied away. If I am wrong about one thing here, the likeliest candidate is AC-1's recipe: the picker's popover-gating is read from source at :627-642, not watched, and if it is wrong the ticket's one behavioural fix goes unverified at QA.
residual_risks: QA goes here first: AC-1 depends on a recipe nobody has driven. Every control exists and the config was executed against the real predicates, but the picker's popover-gating step is read from source rather than watched. If the exhausted fixture does not survive the round trip, AC-1 stalls — and it is the ticket's one behavioural fix.
Nothing in CI runs Playwright, so the four e2e review findings can regress silently. Only AC-3 gates. They are also the only part of this plan no CI test will ever have run.

Duplicate delivery of schedule/skip-next-date — a network retry, a sync re-delivery, a client firing twice — advances next_date twice. The queue guarantees serialisation, not that two calls are the same request. Closing it needs an idempotency key, a feature with its own design questions.
The QA 1 fix hides the menu item rather than surfacing why. A user with an exhausted recurrence who remembers the item gets no explanation. Accepted cost of the rejected alternative.
Two closely-named predicates now coexist with different meanings. Mitigated by doc comments on both functions, but a future reader who collapses them still reintroduces this bug.

review.title: The ticket's one behavioural fix — hiding Skip on an exhausted recurrence — has no test that fails without it. The new e2e test 'hides skip on a one-off schedule and offers it on a recurring one' passes identically on the pre-fix code, and the loot-core unit tests test the new predicate in isolation, never through a menu. Reverting all four skip-eligibility call sites to the old scheduleIsRecurring(dateCond) leaves the entire suite green.
review.detail:
The ticket's one behavioural fix — hiding Skip on an exhausted recurrence — has no test that fails without it. The new e2e test 'hides skip on a one-off schedule and offers it on a recurring one' passes identically on the pre-fix code, and the loot-core unit tests test the new predicate in isolation, never through a menu. Reverting all four skip-eligibility call sites to the old scheduleIsRecurring(dateCond) leaves the entire suite green.

`packages/desktop-client/e2e/schedules.test.ts:378`

Evidence: Executed. (1) Reverted the four call sites — SchedulesTable.tsx:178, ScheduledTransactionMenuModal.tsx:62, SelectedTransactionsButton.tsx:148, useTransactionRowContextActions.ts:107 — each from scheduleIsSkippable(dateCond, <x>.next_date) back to scheduleIsRecurring(dateCond), restarted the dev server cleanly, and ran the suite: E2E_START_URL=http://localhost:3001 npx playwright test schedules.test.ts -g "hides skip" → 1 passed (23.4s). (2) Restored the fix, same command → 1 passed (7.2s); full 7-test suite → 7 passed (45.0s). The test's fixtures cannot discriminate: the one-off is built by oneOffModal.uncheckRepeats(), whose date condition is a plain date so scheduleIsRecurring was ALREADY false for it (that was PR #59's fix), and the recurring fixture is a plain monthly never-ending rule for which getNextDateAfter returns a date under both predicates. Neither fixture is an exhausted recurrence, which is the only input where the two predicates differ. The unit tests at schedules.test.ts:1056-1166 call scheduleIsSkippable directly and so pass whatever the call sites do.

Fix: Add an exhausted-recurrence fixture to the e2e test and assert Skip is absent from it — the same test that already asserts Skip is present on the never-ending recurring row. Build it through the UI the way AC-1's recipe describes: check Repeats, open the picker popover via the recurrence-description button, set repeat_end_dropdown='for' and #end_occurrences=1, Apply. It needs a distinct payee from the existing two so the row can be located, and the recurring assertion must move past it. This also gives AC-5 its first automated footing: today nothing compares the four menus, so a fifth skip site would pass every gate.

review.title: The e2e console assertion was widened well past what the work order asked for; the extra ~50 lines are a self-test of the test rather than a guard on the product. The order said "add a console assertion regex-narrowed to the two React warnings, following command-bar.test.ts:64-95" — that range is `referredText` plus `watchDialogWarnings` and nothing more. The diff instead adds REACT_INPUT_WARNING_PROBES, a loop splitting the regex on `|` asserting each alternative has a matching probe, and a second collector fed by a page.evaluate that console.errors the two literals back into the page. All three prove the filter still matches strings held as constants in the same file.
review.detail:
The e2e console assertion was widened well past what the work order asked for; the extra ~50 lines are a self-test of the test rather than a guard on the product. The order said "add a console assertion regex-narrowed to the two React warnings, following command-bar.test.ts:64-95" — that range is `referredText` plus `watchDialogWarnings` and nothing more. The diff instead adds REACT_INPUT_WARNING_PROBES, a loop splitting the regex on `|` asserting each alternative has a matching probe, and a second collector fed by a page.evaluate that console.errors the two literals back into the page. All three prove the filter still matches strings held as constants in the same file.

`packages/desktop-client/e2e/schedules.test.ts:453`

Evidence: The order names command-bar.test.ts:64-95; I read it and it contains referredText's closing brace (64), watchDialogWarnings (73-82), and the start of test.describe (84) — the probe constants and emission live at :25-49 and :130-165, outside the cited range. In command-bar the probe is load-bearing because DIALOG_WARNING_PROBES is transcribed from a dependency's dist (@radix-ui/react-dialog@1.1.15) and the test must prove the collector matches text it does not own. Here REACT_INPUT_WARNING_PROBES is React's wording, which the guard under test does not produce either way. The comment at :456 concedes the split "would need revisiting" if the pattern changed.

Fix: Keep reactInputWarning, CONSOLE_SETTLE_MS, watchReactInputWarnings, the waitForTimeout drain and expect(messages).toEqual([]). Delete REACT_INPUT_WARNING_PROBES, the alternatives loop, and the trailing probe block — roughly 50 lines. If the self-check is wanted it belongs in a shared helper with the Radix one, out of scope here.

Evidence: watchReactInputWarnings(page) is registered at :379 and the modal is opened twice via schedulesPage.addNewSchedule() (:382, :392) — both the adding path, where useScheduleEdit.ts:266 seeds name: null. It is the edit path specifically that is unproven.

Fix: In the same test, open one of the schedules just created for editing (click its row, or use the existing SchedulesPage/navigation helpers) before the console assertion, so the edit path's render is inside the watched window.

review.title: _openNthScheduleMenu widened to accept a Locator resolves page.getByRole('menu') in strict mode with no disambiguation. This is correct today because only one context menu is mounted, but the wait it adds is the first thing to break if a second role="menu" element ever coexists on a page that runs this suite.
review.detail:
_openNthScheduleMenu widened to accept a Locator resolves page.getByRole('menu') in strict mode with no disambiguation. This is correct today because only one context menu is mounted, but the wait it adds is the first thing to break if a second role="menu" element ever coexists on a page that runs this suite.

`packages/desktop-client/e2e/page-models/schedules-page.ts:115`

Evidence: const menu = this.page.getByRole('menu'); await expect(menu).toBeVisible(); — toBeVisible() is a strict-mode assertion in Playwright and throws on multi-match, whereas the two consumers that read the menu (count() at :75, allTextContents() at :85) tolerate many elements. Menu renders role="menu" (component-library/src/Menu.tsx:161) and the schedules page currently mounts exactly one via ContextMenu.tsx, so all 7 e2e tests pass. The change is an improvement over the prior code, which returned the locator with no wait at all; this is a note on the new coupling, not a defect in current behaviour.

Fix: Scope to the context menu specifically — this.page.getByRole('menu').last(), or a data-testid on the ContextMenu's Menu — so the added wait cannot start failing on an unrelated menu appearing elsewhere on the page.

`packages/desktop-client/e2e/page-models/schedules-page.ts:115`

Evidence: schedules-page.ts:114-115 returns this.page.getByRole('menu') after await expect(menu).toBeVisible(). Playwright's toBeVisible() resolves in strict mode and throws on multi-match; menu.getByRole('button', { name }).count() (:75) and allTextContents() (:85) do not. I checked for an existing convention and there is none to borrow: page.getByRole('menu') appears unscoped in accounts.test.ts:77/90, budget.test.ts:71/78/85, payees.test.ts:64, rules.test.ts:144, reports.test.ts:58 and schedules.test.ts:373 — every existing use is equally unscoped, so this change matches the codebase rather than departing from it.

Fix: Leave as is for consistency with the six other unscoped uses — the wait is still strictly better than the lazy locator it replaces. If you do scope it, scope it repo-wide in one pass rather than only here.
